definitions.gloss: to delay; to postpone; to put off; to set back
definitions.explanation: To make something happen later than originally planned or scheduled. Can refer to deliberately pushing back a schedule or causing something to be late.

examples.japanese: {出発|しゅっぱつ}を{一時間|いちじかん}{遅|おく}らせた。
examples.english: We delayed the departure by one hour.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{開始|かいし}{時間|じかん}を30{分|ぷん}{遅|おく}らしてもいいですか。
examples.english: Can we push the meeting start time back by 30 minutes?

examples.japanese: {悪天候|あくてんこう}のため、{試合|しあい}の{開始|かいし}を{遅|おく}らせざるを{得|え}なかった。
examples.english: Due to bad weather, we had no choice but to delay the start of the match.

notes:
USAGE:
The transitive counterpart of {遅|おく}れる (to be late, intransitive). Used when someone deliberately or actively causes a delay.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出発|しゅっぱつ}を{遅|おく}らす (to delay departure)
- {時間|じかん}を{遅|おく}らす (to push back the time)
- {予定|よてい}を{遅|おく}らす (to postpone a plan)

GRAMMAR:
Godan verb ({遅|おく}らす → {遅|おく}らさない → {遅|おく}らして). Transitive. The intransitive form is {遅|おく}れる. Also written as {遅|おく}らせる (ichidan, causative form of {遅|おく}れる), which is more common in modern usage.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {延期|えんき}する: to postpone — more formal, used for events and official dates
- {先延|さきの}ばしにする: to put off — more casual, often implies procrastination
